## Session Brief

* [F1: a symmetric H → ZZ* split and an α floor, measured on the bbx ladder](F1.md) - Implement the symmetric two-daughter draw for X → VV* splits (default) and an α floor after the survey (selectable), then run bbx at 600k and 1.2M over 20 paired seeds against T1's falsifier and measure every gate the split moves.
* [F2: the α floor on by default, bit-identical where it raises nothing](F2.md) - Make the 1e-4 α floor the default, skip its renormalisation when no α is raised, merge main, and show with a validate pair which banked cells move against F1's split-only tree.
* [T1: where bbx's α-share tail points sit, and why their variance does not fall with points](T1.md) - Record the largest-weight points per channel and iteration on bbx_to_ccx_emmm_qcd0, estimate each heavy channel's tail index, locate the tail points in phase space against the channel's map, and propose a fix verified on the dumps.

## Session Report

* [F1 report: the either-order H → ZZ* split brings bbx's ladder to 0.78, and with an α floor to 0.71](F1-report.md) - Splits with two Breit–Wigner daughters now draw either daughter first with probability ½ (the pair-order map choice, symmetric by default; artifact format 15). An α floor after the survey is selectable and off. On bbx_to_ccx_emmm_qcd0, 20 paired seeds at 600k and 1.2M, the per-seed sd ratio goes from 1.227 (control) to 0.784 (split) and 0.708 (split + floor 1e-4), with χ²/dof at 1.2M of 1.41, 1.18 and 0.66. T1's arithmetic is reproduced through the code on 8 of 8 points. Falsifier (b) and (c) hold on both arms. (a) holds for the on-shell-mirror population T1 described, but fails literally on a third one, both Z pairs off shell on the H peak. (d) misses by about 1σ of the difference, with no consistent sign. The validate pair moves 2 cells for the split (ee_to_mumu_tata_qcd0, pass → pass) and 47 for the forced-on floor (all pass → pass, 41 at the ulp).
* [T1 report: bbx's α-share tails are half-covered H → ZZ* peaks and Z → 4f peaks whose channels the α survey starved](T1-report.md) - On bbx_to_ccx_emmm_qcd0 (20 paired seeds, 600k and 1.2M) the largest single-point contributions sit on two narrow structures. 85% (1.2M) and 46% (600k) of their summed square is the H → ZZ* peak in the half no channel's map covers: every H channel draws the same Z pair first, on its pole, so the configuration with the other pair near shell lies in a Breit–Wigner tail. Seed 55's 1.18e-8 pb point in channel 613 is one of these. Another 11% / 31% is a Z → 4f peak (Z → l l γ*) whose covering channels the α survey drove to α = 1e-11 … 1e-5. A symmetrised H → ZZ* split lowers the mirror points' weights 20–380×, and an α floor of 1e-4 lowers the Z → 4f points 1.0–125×. Together they cut the summed square of the recorded tail contributions to 6% (1.2M) and 25% (600k). Proposed, not implemented, with a falsifier.
* [How MadEvent covers both halves of H → ZZ* in bbx_to_ccx_emmm_qcd0](madevent-hzz-coverage.md) - Read-only study of MadGraph 3.7.1 and this row's MadEvent output: one integration channel per on/off-shell assignment of the Z pair, split by a hard 5Γ cut, so our one-sided H → ZZ* coverage was a deviation.
